title: Matei Zaharia (@matei_zaharia)
clean_title: Reducing cost in agent systems with BRANE's query routing approach
summary:
It is very clear that cost and inefficiency is one of the biggest problem in agent systems now.
Cursor released router that choose models for either cost or performance. Omnigent from Databricks orchestrates between different harnesses. Fugu from Sakana etc.. And many other companies in the agent ecosystem is releasing features somewhat to reduce agent cost.
In BRANE, we work towards reducing cost in agents while preserving quality. Glad to see the community picking up the problem and the idea 🙌
Quoting @diamai_
One agent benchmark cost Melissa Pan's team about $11,000 to profile.
Her 30-minute talk shows why choosing the model is only one part of the route. The system may also need to choose retrieval, document count, summarization, and whether an agent loop runs at all.
03:48 The cheapest and most expensive configurations differed in cost by roughly 1,000x. Exhaustive search is too expensive to repeat for every workload.
09:12 Two nearly identical questions need different pipelines. GLM-5 can answer who Matei Zaharia is from its weights. The same model invents an answer about Melissa until web search is enabled.
20:10 Pan explains BRANE, her system for routing each query to a full agent configuration. It gives every candidate configuration its own classical predictor, then selects the cheapest one likely to meet the accuracy target.
29:05 Across three benchmarks, BRANE was the only tested method that met the 100% static accuracy target on all three while reducing cost. The maximum reduction was 89%.
BRANE uses roughly 150 to 600 profiled queries per configuration. Most teams need a manual router before they have that history.
The article below starts there, with a fixed task card, proof, retry cap, and permission ceiling. Each comparable run adds a row to the ledger.
That ledger is the training data for the router you may automate later.
🎬 https://pbs.twimg.com/amplify_video_thumb/2077792577500106752/img/6F6KOYin8WzGfi--.jpg | https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2077792577500106752/vid/avc1/480x270/1BIVcnEkIup2H0xn.mp4?tag=29
clean_summary:
Cost and inefficiency are major challenges in current agent systems. Tools like Cursor, Omnigent, and Fugu aim to optimize model selection for either cost or performance, while BRANE works to reduce agent costs without sacrificing quality by intelligently routing queries to configurations likely to meet accuracy targets at lower costs.

Melissa Pan's team highlights that profiling a single agent configuration can cost around $11,000, and choosing the right system involves more than just model selection, including retrieval, document count, and summarization choices. BRANE's approach uses profiling data from a limited number of queries to predict the most cost-effective configuration, achieving up to 89% cost reduction while maintaining 100% accuracy across benchmarks. This method relies on building a ledger of configurations and their performance, which can later be used to automate routing decisions.

summary:
AI-based research and engineering is one of the main topics we're researching in the STAR Lab at Berkeley, and something I'm seeing used in industry more and more too. This is nice work from my grad students packaging multiple AI-based "autoresearch" algorithms into one API in the GEPA package so you can mix-and-match them to get the best results. These can be used for anything from writing prompts to designing agents to optimizing code.
Quoting @ShangyinT
Many LLM-based optimization algorithms have been proposed recently. We find that GEPA, AutoResearch, and Meta-Harness each win on different tasks and no single LLM optimizer wins everywhere.
How do we leverage the complementary performance profiles of these optimization algorithms?
Today, we release optimize_anything omni: a meta-optimizer that leverages the best of each optimizer. At a matched budget, omni beats every standalone optimizer. (thread)
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HN7MBFWakAAr6Md.jpg
clean_summary:
AI-based research and engineering is a key focus at Berkeley's STAR Lab and is increasingly used in industry. The work introduces the GEPA package, which packages multiple AI-based autoresearch algorithms into one API, allowing users to mix and match them for optimal results in tasks like writing prompts, designing agents, and optimizing code.

A recent development is optimize_anything omni, a meta-optimizer that leverages the strengths of different AI optimization algorithms. It outperforms each standalone optimizer at a given budget by combining their capabilities, demonstrating the benefit of using complementary profiles of these algorithms.
